NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The builders must move the great stone for the new hearth: make up a work song, or use rollers and ropes.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The new hearth stone is enormous, and it has to be moved from the beach to the meeting hut. (subject) wants everyone to pull on ropes to a work song, all together. (friend) has worked out a system of log rollers that might make it easy. What should they try?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Forty villagers pull on ropes to (subject)'s song. The stone moves a stride with every chorus. It takes all day. Everyone's hands are raw and everyone is singing.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend)'s rollers work beautifully, and the stone glides up the beach. Then the slope begins, and it glides back down. In the end, they use the rollers and the song.
